historical_timeline.summary: Two operations for benign breast cysts at Mount Sinai Hospital.
Admitted to Doctor's Hospital in New York with psychoneurosis.
Possible first signs of macular degeneration (retrospective suggestion).
Loses central vision; keeps only peripheral sight.
Last unassisted oil painting; letter describing a cloudy left eye.
Died at St. Vincent's Hospital, Santa Fe.

claims.statement: Georgia Totto O'Keeffe was born on November 15, 1887, to Francis Calyxtus O'Keeffe and Ida Totto O'Keeffe at the family dairy farm near Sun Prairie, Wisconsin, the second of seven children.
O'Keeffe died at St. Vincent's Hospital in Santa Fe, New Mexico, on March 6, 1986, at age 98.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Record the death as a fact without graphic detail.

claims.statement: O'Keeffe's mother died in Charlottesville, Virginia, in May 1916, and her father died in Petersburg, Virginia, in November 1918.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The cited chronology does not give causes of death.

claims.statement: In 1927 O'Keeffe was admitted twice to Mount Sinai Hospital in New York for surgery to remove benign breast cysts.
In February 1933 O'Keeffe was admitted to Doctor's Hospital in New York, suffering from psychoneurosis, and recuperated in Bermuda in March and April.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The period term is kept as recorded; no modern psychiatric diagnosis is inferred.

claims.statement: O'Keeffe's eyesight began to fail in 1968.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The documented anchor for the synthetic presentation of macular degeneration.

claims.statement: Early in 1971 O'Keeffe lost her central vision and kept only peripheral sight; the O'Keeffe Museum and the Whitney Museum attribute her vision loss to macular degeneration.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The type of macular degeneration (dry or neovascular) was not recorded in the sources.

claims.statement: O'Keeffe completed her last unassisted oil painting in 1972 and continued in oil with assistance until 1977; she worked unassisted in watercolor and charcoal until 1978 and in graphite until 1984. From 1973 the potter Juan Hamilton was her assistant, and from 1974 he taught her to work in clay.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Shows adaptation to low vision; the modern episode uses it to frame vision rehabilitation.

source_links.locator: Watercolors made with assistants in her early eighties

claims.statement: In a 1972 letter O'Keeffe wrote that her left eye had become much more cloudy and that her right eye seemed to be beginning to cloud.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Quoted in a secondary source from a 1992 biography; the letter itself was not reviewed. Suggests the left eye was affected first.

source_links.locator: Quotes the 1972 letter as cited in Hogrefe's 1992 biography

claims.statement: The first signs of O'Keeffe's macular degeneration may have appeared as early as 1964.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Retrospective suggestion by an advocacy site; not documented in the museum chronology.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Recognize new distortion in one eye as a possible sign of neovascular age-related macular degeneration that needs ophthalmology evaluation within days; follow intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment with acuity, OCT, and pressure checks under the AAO Preferred Practice Pattern; protect the fellow eye with AREDS2 supplements and home Amsler grid monitoring; and support function, safety, and mood with low-vision rehabilitation, in an artist whose central vision was lost before these treatments existed.
